findings.finding: RingCentral has beaten the top of its own guide on the last two prints. Q1 2026 revenue was $644M against a $640-645M guide; Q2 was $657M against $648-653M (+$4M over the top), with EPS $1.22 against $1.15-1.17. Repeating the Q2 pattern on the $664-670M / $1.25-1.30 Q3 guide gives about $671-673M and EPS about $1.31-1.33, roughly 0.6% over the $667M consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 beat at the top of the guide with a FY raise moved +0.53%. The Q3 2025 beat with a FY midpoint cut moved -8.25%. The beat itself has not driven the stock; guidance and AI metrics have.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a top-of-range beat is this company's habit and consensus already sits at the guide midpoint to top. If the market expected a larger beat, consensus would sit above the guide top; it sits at about $667M, inside the range.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001384905/000138490526000033/rng-20260331x8kxex991.htm) is a separate document showing the same beat-the-top habit. Both are company documents.

findings.finding: The company's own Q3 guide implies YoY growth decelerating against a tough comp. Q3 2025 had an unusually large sequential subscriptions step (about $599M to $616M, +$17M), against about +$11M a quarter in 2026 ($623M to $634M). At the guide midpoint, total growth is about 4.4% ($667M vs $639M) and subscriptions growth about 4.9%, against 5.9% / 5.8% in Q2. Even a $4M beat prints about 5.1% total growth. The implied Q4 is about 4.4%. This sits on a stock whose rally was framed as AI-driven re-acceleration; Needham says acceleration is a 2027 story not in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Growth deceleration and a guidance cut in Q3 2025 brought -8.25% (Seeking Alpha 2025-11-04, 'RingCentral slides after lowering midpoint of full-year 2025 revenue guidance'). Growth at 5.9% with AI metrics brought +25.09% in July 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company's own guide, so mostly priced for anyone who did the comp arithmetic. If the headline 'growth slows to ~5%' were fully absorbed, the stock would not have run +9% in five days to a 52-week high on an acceleration narrative. Sized small because the guide told the market.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 revenue $639M and subscriptions $616M come from the separate Q3 2025 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251103123510/en). The Needham note (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/needham-raises-ringcentral-stock-price-target-on-growth-outlook-93CH-4881249) says acceleration is not in the current guide. Same company guide document as finding 1.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide has been raised at every print this year: the Q1 release set revenue at $2.62-2.64B and EPS at $4.85-5.01, and the Q2 release raised these to $2.635-2.646B, EPS $4.96-5.10 and FCF $615-625M. The FY guide implies Q4 revenue of about $672M, about 4.4% YoY, which leaves room for another raise if Q3 beats by $4-5M. Q3 also brings the first look at the 2027 trajectory that Needham's CFO meetings pointed to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line decides this stock. FY midpoint cut (Nov 2025): -8.25%. Raise plus AI metrics plus dividend (Feb 2026): +34.4%. Raise (May 2026): +0.53%. Raise across all metrics (Jul 2026): +25.09%.
findings.why_not_priced: A raise is expected after a 3x run; a raise above the Q3 beat would be the unpriced part. The skew is only +3.5 and the implied move is 11.8%, so options do not price a clear direction.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001384905/000138490526000033/rng-20260331x8kxex991.htm) for the earlier guide; Needham note on 2027 acceleration (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/needham-raises-ringcentral-stock-price-target-on-growth-outlook-93CH-4881249).

findings.finding: AI adoption metrics are strong and peers that reported after RingCentral last spoke corroborate AI voice demand. RingCentral at Q2: more than 16,000 paying AI Receptionist customers (+400% YoY), ACE more than 6,300 (+70%), AI-paying customers about 13% of ARR (doubled YoY), AI-led new-product ARR up nearly 60% in H1, and over half of new sales including AI. After 2026-07-23, 8x8 (2026-08-04) reported AI adoption +121% and usage revenue +63% and raised its FY outlook. Zoom (2026-08-25) reported enterprise growth of 7.8%, its best in three years, Zoom Virtual Agent customers +256%, and record CX deals with paid AI in 9 of its top 10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The AI metric disclosures accompanied the +34.4% (Feb 2026) and +25.09% (Jul 2026) reactions. In Nov 2025, analysts said AI products had not attracted new customers and the stock fell 8.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the AI story is why the stock tripled. The unpriced part is the size of the next AIR/AI ARR step. If the market had priced a disappointment, the skew would be far more put-heavy than +3.5.
findings.independence: The peer metrics are a proxy, not RingCentral numbers. 8x8 Q1 FY27 (https://www.8x8.com/newsroom/8x8-inc-reports-record-revenue-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027, 2026-08-04); Zoom Q2 FY27 (https://investors.zoom.us/news-releases/news-release-details/zoom-communications-reports-financial-results-second-quarter-0, 2026-08-25).

findings.finding: Capital return capacity is close to running out and could be refreshed. Q2 bought back 2.2M shares for $94M, leaving about $326M under the authorization (about 3.5 quarters at that pace). The dividend was raised 67% to $0.125. Gross debt is falling toward a $1B year-end target with net leverage at 1.5x. A new authorization or another dividend step at this print is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend initiation came with the Feb 2026 +34.4% move; the dividend raise came with the Jul 2026 +25.09% move. Both were bundled with guidance raises, so they cannot be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: A refreshed authorization is not announced; with about $326M left the timing is open. Small.
findings.independence: GuruFocus call highlights (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8976665/...) on debt reduction to $1B and the 1.5x net leverage. Same quarter's disclosures.

findings.finding: There were service incidents in the quarter on the contact-center product. On 2026-09-24, Americas Contact Center inbound and outbound calls were disrupted for about 4.4 hours and EMEA inbound for about 1.8 hours. Americas call routing was hit on 2026-09-03/04 for about 3.5 hours. On 2026-09-30 a 36-minute Americas registration/call-drop incident hit RingEX. All were classified minor and resolved.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of incidents moving a print; the Jan 2025 outage did not show up in the reported quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Not aggregated by any preview, but these are minor incidents on a contact-center product that is a small share of revenue. Near-zero effect.
